5.1.1
Adding the dagger structure

It remains to construct the
{\dagger}
-structure
r
and the state
\psi_{\mathcal{P}}
on
{\mathcal{P}}
, satisfying the conditions listed in Definition
4.5
.

Definition 5.1
.

For
n\geq 0
, we define
r_{n}:{\mathcal{P}}[n]\to\overline{{\mathcal{P}}[n]}
to be the composite

\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(x^{\otimes n})\xrightarrow{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(r_{x}^{\otimes n})}\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\overline{x}^{\otimes n})\xrightarrow{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\nu)}\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\overline{x^{\otimes n}})\xrightarrow{\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}}_{x^{\otimes n}}}\overline{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(x^{\otimes n})}.

Lemma 5.2
.

\overline{r_{n}}\circ r_{n}=\varphi_{{\mathcal{P}}[n]}
.

Proof.

Going right and then down in the following commutative diagram is
\overline{r_{n}}\circ r_{n}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\overline{x}^{\otimes n})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\overline{x^{\otimes n}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(x^{\otimes n})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(x^{\otimes n})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\overline{\overline{x}}^{\otimes n})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\overline{\overline{x}^{\otimes n}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\overline{x}^{\otimes n})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\overline{\overline{x^{\otimes n}}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\overline{x^{\otimes n}})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{\overline{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(x^{\otimes n})}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\overline{r_{x}}^{\otimes n})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\nu)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}}_{x^{\otimes n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\overline{r_{x}^{\otimes n}})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(r_{x}^{\otimes n})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(r_{x}^{\otimes n})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\varphi_{x}^{\otimes n})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\varphi_{x^{\otimes n}})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi_{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(x^{\otimes n})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\nu)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}}_{\overline{x}^{\otimes n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\overline{\nu})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\nu)}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}}_{\overline{x^{\otimes n}}}}
Prop.
2.21
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}}_{x^{\otimes n}}}}

This is equal to the curved arrow
\varphi_{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(x^{\otimes n})}=\varphi_{{\mathcal{P}}[n]}
.
∎

Proposition 5.3
.

The pair
({\mathcal{P}},r)
satisfies
(P1)
:

\overline{Z(T)}\circ\nu^{(k)}\circ(r_{n_{k}}\otimes\cdots\otimes r_{n_{1}})=r_{n_{0}}\circ Z(\overline{T}).

(When
k=0
,
\overline{Z(T)}\circ r_{\mathcal{V}}=r_{n_{0}}\circ Z(\overline{T})
where
r_{\mathcal{V}}:1_{\mathcal{V}}\to\overline{1_{\mathcal{V}}}
is the real structure of
1_{\mathcal{V}}
.)

is involutive lax monoidal by Proposition

.

}{{{{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \lxSVG@transformcm{1.0}{0.0}{0.0}{1.0}{9.96646pt}{17.39673pt}\lxSVG@begingroup@{transform} \pgfsys@hbox{60}\lxSVG@closescope }}}
\lxSVG@closescope }}}
\lxSVG@closescope {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}\hss}\lxSVG@discardpath\lxSVG@closescope \hss}}\lxSVG@closescope\endpgfpicture}}}}\,.

First, since
\overline{u}=u
, by unitality,

\overline{Z(u)}\circ r_{\mathcal{V}}=\overline{i}\circ r_{\mathcal{V}}=\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}}_{1}\circ\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(r_{\mathcal{C}})\circ i=r_{0}\circ Z(\overline{u}).

Since
\overline{m_{i,j}}=m_{j,i}
,
by monoidality,

\displaystyle\overline{Z(m_{i,j})}\circ\nu\circ(r_{j}\otimes r_{i})

\displaystyle=\overline{\mu_{i,j}}\circ\nu\circ\big((\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}}_{x^{\otimes j}}\circ\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\nu)\circ\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(r_{x}^{\otimes j}))\otimes(\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}}_{x^{\otimes i}}\circ\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\nu)\circ\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(r_{x}^{\otimes i}))\big)

\displaystyle=\overline{\mu_{i,j}}\circ\nu\circ(\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}}_{x^{\otimes j}}\otimes\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}}_{x^{\otimes i}})\circ(\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\nu)\otimes\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\nu))\circ(\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(r_{x}^{\otimes j})\otimes\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(r_{x}^{\otimes i}))

\displaystyle=\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}}_{x^{\otimes i+j}}\circ\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\nu)\circ\mu_{\overline{x^{\otimes j}},\overline{x^{\otimes i}}}\circ(\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\nu)\otimes\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\nu))\circ(\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(r_{x}^{\otimes j})\otimes\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(r_{x}^{\otimes i}))

\displaystyle=\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}}_{x^{\otimes i+j}}\circ\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\nu)\circ\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(r_{x}^{\otimes i+j})\circ\mu_{j,i}

\displaystyle=r_{i+j}\circ Z(\overline{m_{i,j}}).

The third equality above uses the lax involutive property of
\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}
, and the fourth equality uses naturality of
\mu
.
Since
\overline{a_{i}}=a_{n-i}
(when
Z(a_{i}):\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(x^{\otimes n+2})\to\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(x^{\otimes n})
), we see

\displaystyle\overline{Z(a_{i})}\circ r_{n+2}

\displaystyle=\overline{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\id_{x^{\otimes i}}\otimes\ev_{x}\otimes x^{\otimes n-i})}\circ\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}}_{x^{\otimes n+2}}\circ\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\nu)\circ\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(r_{x}^{\otimes n+2})

\displaystyle=\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}}_{x^{\otimes n}}\circ\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\nu)\circ\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(r_{x}^{\otimes n})\circ\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\id_{x^{\otimes n-i}}\otimes\ev_{x}\otimes x^{\otimes i})

\displaystyle=r_{n}\circ Z(a_{n-i}).

The proof for the
a_{i}^{\dagger}
is similar and omitted.
(It also follows formally from the proof for
a_{i}
as
\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}
is a dagger functor and
\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}}
,
r
,
\nu
, and
r_{x}
are all unitary.)
Finally, for the tangles
t_{i,j}
, we have
\overline{t_{i,j}}=t_{i,j}^{-1}
, and by Lemma
3.13
,

\displaystyle\overline{Z(t_{i,j})}\circ r_{n}

\displaystyle=\overline{\tau_{i,j}}\circ\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}}_{x^{\otimes n}}\circ\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\nu)\circ\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(r_{x}^{\otimes n})

\displaystyle=\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}}_{x^{\otimes n}}\circ\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\nu)\circ\tau^{-1}_{\overline{x}^{\otimes i},\overline{x}^{\otimes j}}\circ\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(r_{x}^{\otimes n})

\displaystyle=\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}}_{x^{\otimes n}}\circ\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(\nu)\circ\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(r_{x}^{\otimes n})\circ\tau^{-1}_{x^{\otimes i},x^{\otimes j}}

\displaystyle=r_{n}\circ Z(\overline{t_{i,j}}).\qed

Definition 5.4
.

We define a state
\psi_{\mathcal{P}}:=i^{\dagger}:{\mathcal{P}}[0]\to 1_{\mathcal{V}}
as in §
3.3
.

satisfies
(P2)

5.1.2
Functoriality

Suppose
G=(G,\gamma):({\mathcal{C}}_{1},\Phi_{1}^{\scriptscriptstyle{\mathcal{Z}}},\vee_{1},\psi_{1},x_{1})\to({\mathcal{C}}_{2},\Phi_{2}^{\scriptscriptstyle{\mathcal{Z}}},\vee_{2},\psi_{2},x_{2})
is a 1-morphism of pointed unitary module multitensor categories over
{\mathcal{V}}
.
(Recall that
\gamma
is a family of unitary isomorphisms
\gamma_{v}:\Phi_{2}(v)\to G(\Phi_{1}(v))
.)

Let
({\mathcal{P}}_{i},r^{i},\psi_{i})=\Lambda({\mathcal{C}}_{i},\Phi_{i}^{\scriptscriptstyle{\mathcal{Z}}},\vee_{i},\psi_{i},x_{i})
be the unitary anchored algebra constructed in the previous subsection for
i=1,2
.
In
[
HPT23b
, §5.3]
, we obtained a map of ordinary anchored planar algebras
\Lambda(G):{\mathcal{P}}_{1}\to{\mathcal{P}}_{2}

as follows.

•

First, for each
c\in{\mathcal{C}}_{1}
, we define
\zeta_{c}:\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}(c)\to\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{2}(G(c))
to be the mate of

\Phi_{2}(\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}(c))\xrightarrow{\gamma_{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}(c)}}G(\Phi_{1}(\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}(c)))\xrightarrow{G(\varepsilon_{c}^{1})}G(c)

under the unitary adjunction
\Phi_{2}\dashv\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{2}
.

•

The map
\Lambda(G):{\mathcal{P}}_{1}\to{\mathcal{P}}_{2}
associated to
G:({\mathcal{C}}_{1},x_{1})\to({\mathcal{C}}_{2},x_{2})
is the sequence of morphisms

\Lambda(G)[n]:{\mathcal{P}}_{1}[n]\to{\mathcal{P}}_{2}[n]

given by

\Lambda(G)[n]\,:\,{\mathcal{P}}_{1}[n]=\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}(x_{1}^{\otimes n})\xrightarrow{\,\,\,\,\textstyle\zeta_{x_{1}^{\otimes n}}\,\,\,}\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{2}(G(x_{1}^{\otimes n}))\xrightarrow{\cong}\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{2}(x_{2}^{\otimes n})={\mathcal{P}}_{2}[n].

It remains to prove that
\Lambda(G)
is compatible with
r_{n}
and
\psi
, i.e.,

\displaystyle\overline{\Lambda(G)[n]}\circ r_{n}^{1}

\displaystyle=r_{n}^{2}\circ\Lambda(G)[n]

\displaystyle\forall\,n\geq 0

(27)

\displaystyle\text{and}\quad\psi_{1}

\displaystyle=\psi_{2}\circ\Lambda(G)[0].

(28)

Equation (
27
) is checked by the following commutative diagram.

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}^{1}_{\mathcal{V}}(x_{1}^{\otimes n})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}^{1}_{\mathcal{V}}(\overline{x_{1}}^{\otimes n})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}^{1}_{\mathcal{V}}(\overline{x_{1}^{\otimes n}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{\mathbf{Tr}^{1}_{\mathcal{V}}(x_{1}^{\otimes n})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{2}(G(x_{1}^{\otimes n}))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{2}(G(\overline{x_{1}}^{\otimes n}))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{2}(G(\overline{x_{1}^{\otimes n}}))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{2}(\overline{G(x_{1}^{\otimes n})})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{2}(G(x_{1}^{\otimes n}))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{2}(x_{2}^{\otimes n})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{2}(\overline{x_{2}}^{\otimes n})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{2}(\overline{x_{2}^{\otimes n}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{2}(x_{2}^{\otimes n})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}^{1}_{\mathcal{V}}(r_{x_{1}}^{\otimes n})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta_{x_{1}^{\otimes n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}^{1}_{\mathcal{V}}(\nu)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta_{\overline{x_{1}}^{\otimes n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}^{1}_{\mathcal{V}}}_{x_{1}^{\otimes n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\zeta_{\overline{x_{1}^{\otimes n}}}}
(Lem.
5.7
)
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{\zeta_{x_{1}^{\otimes n}}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}^{2}_{\mathcal{V}}(G(r_{x_{1}}^{\otimes n}))}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}^{2}_{\mathcal{V}}(G(\nu))}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}^{2}_{\mathcal{V}}(\chi^{G}_{x_{1}^{\otimes n}})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}^{2}_{\mathcal{V}}}_{G(x_{1}^{\otimes n})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cong}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}^{2}_{\mathcal{V}}(r_{x_{2}}^{\otimes n})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathbf{Tr}^{2}_{\mathcal{V}}(\nu)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}^{2}_{\mathcal{V}}}_{x_{2}^{\otimes n}}}

Lemma 5.7
.

The natural transformation
\zeta:\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}\Rightarrow\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{2}\circ G
is involutive, i.e., for all
c\in{\mathcal{C}}_{1}
,

\overline{\zeta_{c}}\circ\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}}_{c}=\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{2}}_{G(c)}\circ\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{2}(\chi^{G}_{c})\circ\zeta_{\overline{c}}
.

Proof.

We prove the equivalent relation:

(\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{2}}_{G(c)})^{-1}\circ\overline{\zeta_{c}}=\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{2}(\chi^{G}_{c})\circ\zeta_{\overline{c}}\circ(\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}}_{c})^{-1}.

To do so, we take mates under the adjunction

{\mathcal{V}}(\overline{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}(c)}\to\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{2}(\overline{G(c)}))\cong{\mathcal{C}}_{1}(\Phi_{2}(\overline{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}(c)})\to\overline{G(c)}).

In the commutative diagram below, the mate of the left hand side above is going down and then right, and the mate of the right hand side is going right and then down.

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Phi_{2}(\overline{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}(c)})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Phi_{2}(\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}(\overline{c}))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(\Phi_{1}(\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}(\overline{c})))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(\Phi_{1}(\overline{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}(c)}))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(\overline{\Phi_{1}(\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}(c))})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(\overline{c})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{\Phi_{2}(\mathbf{Tr}^{1}_{\mathcal{V}}(c))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{G(\Phi_{1}(\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}(c)))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Phi_{2}(\overline{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{2}(G(c))})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{\Phi_{2}(\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{2}(G(c)))}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{G(c)}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Phi_{2}(\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}}_{c})^{-1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\gamma_{\overline{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}(c)}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\chi^{\Phi_{2}}_{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}(c)}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Phi_{2}(\overline{\zeta_{c}})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\gamma_{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}(\overline{c})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(\varepsilon_{\overline{c}}^{1})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(\Phi_{1}(\chi^{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}}_{c}))^{-1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(\chi^{\Phi_{1}}_{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}(c)})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G(\overline{\varepsilon^{1}_{c}})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\chi^{G}_{\Phi_{1}(\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}(c))}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\chi^{G}_{c}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{\gamma_{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{1}(c)}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{\Phi_{2}(\zeta_{c})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{G(\varepsilon^{1}_{c})}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\chi^{\Phi_{2}}_{\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}^{2}(G(c))}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{\varepsilon^{2}_{G(c)}}}

The pentagon in the diagram above is the involutivity axiom for
\gamma
.
∎

Checking (
28
) is straightforward.
By Lemma
3.7
,

\psi_{j}
on
\End_{{\mathcal{C}}_{j}}(1_{{\mathcal{C}}_{j}})
is identified with
i_{j}^{\dagger}\circ-
on
\Hom_{\mathcal{V}}(1\to{\mathcal{P}}_{j}[0])
under the isomorphism (
16
),
which is exactly
\psi_{j}
on
{\mathcal{P}}_{j}
by Definition
5.4
.
Since
\psi_{1}=\psi_{2}\circ G
on
\End_{{\mathcal{C}}_{1}}(1_{{\mathcal{C}}_{1}})
, the result follows.

5.2
From unitary anchored planar algebras to unitary module tensor categories

Given a unitary anchored planar algebra
({\mathcal{P}},r,\psi_{\mathcal{P}})
in
{\mathcal{V}}
, we begin by constructing an ordinary pivotal module tensor category
({\mathcal{C}},\Phi^{\scriptscriptstyle{\mathcal{Z}}})
as in
[
HPT23b
, §6]
.
First, we construct a full subcategory
{\mathcal{C}}_{0}
, and we obtain
{\mathcal{C}}
by taking the Cauchy completion.

•

Objects in
{\mathcal{C}}_{0}
are formal symbols
``\Phi(v)\otimes x^{\otimes n}"
for
v\in{\mathcal{V}}
and
n\geq 0
.

•

Hom spaces are defined by

{\mathcal{C}}_{0}(``\Phi(u)\otimes x^{\otimes k}"\to``\Phi(v)\otimes x^{\otimes n}"):={\mathcal{V}}(u\to v\otimes{\mathcal{P}}[n+k]).

Moreover, the identity map

{\mathcal{C}}\big(\Phi(u)\to``\Phi(v)\otimes x^{\otimes n}"\big)={\mathcal{V}}\big(u\to v\otimes{\mathcal{P}}[n]\big)={\mathcal{V}}\big(u\to\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}(``\Phi(v)\otimes x^{\otimes n}")\big)

witnesses the adjunction
\Phi\dashv\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}
.

.

r_{x}:x\to x^{\vee}
is the identity map.

5.2.1
Adding the dagger structure

It remains to perform the following tasks:

(C1)

construct a dagger structure on
{\mathcal{C}}
making it a unitary multitensor category

(C2)

construct a faithful state
\psi_{\mathcal{C}}
on
\End_{\mathcal{C}}(1_{\mathcal{C}})
,

(C3)

check that
\vee_{\mathcal{C}}
is a unitary dual functor and that
the canonical unitary pivotal structure induced by
\vee_{\mathcal{C}}
is
\varphi^{\mathcal{C}}
.

(C4)

check that
r_{x}:x\to x^{\vee}
is a real structure.

(C5)

check that the adjunction
\Phi\dashv\mathbf{Tr}_{\mathcal{V}}
is unitary.

(29)

It is straightforward to verify that
f^{**}=f
for all morphisms

.
To check the remainder of involutivity, we see that
*
on the composite

``\Phi(u)\otimes x^{\otimes k}"\xrightarrow{f}``\Phi(v)\otimes x^{\otimes n}"\xrightarrow{g}``\Phi(w)\otimes x^{\otimes p}"

is given by

Corollary 5.14

(
(C4)
)
.

The symmetric self-duality
r_{x}:x\to x^{\vee}
is unitary, i.e.,
(x,r_{x})
is real.

Proof.

We used the identification between
1_{\mathcal{V}}^{\vee}=1_{\mathcal{V}}
to identify
x=x^{\vee}
and
r_{x}=\id_{x}
, but the former identification is unitary, so the latter is too.
∎

Recall from Lemma
2.17
that
sphericality of the unitary dual functor
\vee_{\mathcal{V}}

is a necessary condition for
the state
\psi_{\mathcal{C}}
to be spherical.

Proposition 5.15
.

If
\vee_{\mathcal{V}}
is a spherical unitary dual functor on
{\mathcal{V}}
and
({\mathcal{P}},j,\psi_{\mathcal{P}})
is spherical, then so is
\psi_{\mathcal{C}}
.

by

.

(

where the action-coherence morphism
\gamma^{\Delta(H)}:\Phi_{2}\Rightarrow\Delta(H)\circ\Phi_{1}
is the identity.

It remains to prove that:

•

\Delta(H)
is a
{\dagger}
-tensor functor,

•

the identity action coherence monoidal natural isomorphism
\id:\Phi_{2}\Rightarrow\Delta(H)\circ\Phi_{1}
is involutive,
i.e.,
for all
v\in{\mathcal{V}}
,

\chi^{\Phi_{2}}_{v}=\chi^{\Delta(H)}_{\Phi_{1}(v)}\circ\Delta(H)(\chi^{\Phi_{1}}_{v}):\Phi_{2}(\overline{v})\to\overline{\Delta(H)(\Phi_{1}(v))}
,
and

•

\psi_{2}\circ\Delta(H)=\psi_{1}
on
\End_{{\mathcal{C}}_{1}}(1_{{\mathcal{C}}_{1}})
.

For the first condition, since
\Delta(H)
is strict, it suffices to check it is a
{\dagger}
-functor.

5.3
Equivalence

Fix a braided unitary tensor category
{\mathcal{V}}
with a choice of unitary dual functor
\vee_{\mathcal{V}}
.
For this section, we use the following notation.

•

\mathsf{APA}
is the 1-category of anchored planar algebras over
{\mathcal{V}}
,
and
\mathsf{UAPA}
is the 1-subcategory of unitary anchored planar algebras over
{\mathcal{V}}
.

•

\mathsf{ModTens}
is the 1-truncation of the 2-category of pointed pivotal module tensor categories over
{\mathcal{V}}
,
and

\mathsf{UModTens}
is the 1-truncation of the 2-category of pointed unitary module multitensor categories over
{\mathcal{V}}
.

In
[
HPT23b
]
, we constructed functors
\Delta:\mathsf{APA}\to\mathsf{ModTens}
and
\Lambda:\mathsf{ModTens}\to\mathsf{APA}
.
In §
5.2.2
above, we showed
\Delta
extends to a functor
\mathsf{UAPA}\to\mathsf{UModTens}
,
and
in §
5.1.2
above, we showed
\Lambda
extends to a functor
\mathsf{UModTens}\to\mathsf{UAPA}
.
Moreover, these extensions are clearly compatible with the forgetful functors which forget our extra unitary structure.

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{UAPA}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{UModTens}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{APA}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{ModTens}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Forget}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Delta}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Forget}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Lambda}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Delta}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Lambda}

In
[
HPT23b
, §7]
, we showed that
\Lambda\circ\Delta=\id_{\mathsf{APA}}
, and it is immediate that
\Lambda\circ\Delta=\id_{\mathsf{UAPA}}
upstairs.
We also constructed a natural isomorphism
\Psi:\Delta\circ\Lambda\Rightarrow\id_{\mathsf{ModTens}}
by

\Psi(f)=\hbox to119.17pt{\vbox to64.73pt{\pgfpicture\makeatletter\hbox{\hskip 64.13448pt\lower-20.88591pt\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke} \lxSVG@begingroup@{fill} \lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\nullfont\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \lxSVG@closescope \hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} {{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}
;
;

\lxSVG@closescope

{}{}}}{

{{}{{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}}{{}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}{}{{}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces
}{{{{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \lxSVG@transformcm{1.0}{0.0}{0.0}{1.0}{-56.99338pt}{37.18887pt}\lxSVG@begingroup@{transform} \pgfsys@hbox{60}\lxSVG@closescope }}}

\lxSVG@closescope {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}\hss}\lxSVG@discardpath\lxSVG@closescope \hss}}\lxSVG@closescope\endpgfpicture}}\qquad\qquad\begin{aligned} f&\in{\mathcal{C}}^{\prime}\big(``\Phi(u)\otimes x^{\otimes i}"\to``\Phi(v)\otimes x^{\otimes j}"\big)\\
&\hskip 28.45274pt={\mathcal{V}}\big(u\to v\otimes{\mathcal{P}}[i+j]\big).\end{aligned}

where
{\mathcal{C}}^{\prime}=\Lambda(\Delta({\mathcal{C}}))
, which is the unitary Cauchy completion of
{\mathcal{C}}^{\prime}_{0}
(recall
{\mathcal{C}}_{0}^{\prime}
has objects
``\Phi(v)\otimes x^{\otimes n}"
for
v\in{\mathcal{V}}
).

It remains to show that
\Psi
lifts to a unitary natural isomorphism upstairs.
To do so, it is enough (in view of the fact that
\Psi
is an isomorphism) to show that
f\mapsto\Psi(f)
is norm-preserving, i.e.,

\big\|f\big\|_{{\mathcal{V}}(u\to v\otimes{\mathcal{P}}[i+j])}=\big\|\Psi(f)\big\|_{{\mathcal{C}}(\Phi(u)\otimes x^{\otimes i}\to\Phi(v)\otimes x^{\otimes j})}.

By replacing
f
by
\ev_{v}\circ(1_{\overline{v}}\otimes f)
(i.e. folding the
v
strand to the left), we may assume without loss of generality that
v=1_{\mathcal{V}}
.
Similarly, by replacing

f\in{\mathcal{C}}^{\prime}\big(``\Phi(u)\otimes x^{\otimes i}"\to``\Phi(v)\otimes x^{\otimes j}"\big)

by the corresponding morphism in
{\mathcal{C}}^{\prime}\big(``\Phi(u)\otimes x^{\otimes 0}"\to``\Phi(v)\otimes x^{\otimes i+j}"\big)
, we may assume without loss of generality that
i=0
.
We may now proceed as in the proof of Proposition
3.9
to show:
